CREWS: this session is a MEMBER for name "audit-test-member" (crew="audit-test-crew").

Your crew: audit-test-crew (multiple orchestrators with disjoint crews can co-exist in this workspace without colliding).

For any crew info — yours or others' — use the `/crews-*` slash commands listed below.
`/crews-status` shows your own state.
## Listener (managed by hooks)

The crews plugin runs a background listener that watches your mailbox and writes
a heartbeat to your manifest. Do NOT arm the listener pre-emptively. The Stop
and PreToolUse hooks will block your turn or your next tool call with the exact
bash command and mode: "async" IF you actually need to arm — that block is the
only signal that asks you to arm.

When the background listener task exits (after delivering mail, timing out, or
detecting an existing listener), IMMEDIATELY inspect its output with read_bash
before any other tool call. Read the JSON envelope to see what happened:
  - {type: "messages", count: N, ...}   — mail delivered; run /crews-review-mail
  - {type: "timeout", waitedMs: N, ...} — timed out; arm a new listener if work continues
  - {type: "arm-skipped", reason: "already-active-listener", existingPid: N, ...}
      — you already have a live listener (existingPid). Do NOT arm a new one.
      The current listener is fine.
  - {type: "error", error: "..."}       — listener crashed; report and arm again

If type === arm-skipped, do NOT re-arm.
If the hook supplies an arm command, use the bash tool with mode: "async" exactly
as provided, then keep the shellId so you can inspect it with read_bash when it
exits. NEVER re-arm a listener without inspecting the previous task output first.
The arm-skipped envelope is the signal that prevents an arm-loop.

EVERY TURN HAS TWO PARTS, IN STRICT ORDER:

  1. Write your normal prose response. Status updates, answers,
     questions, code-change summaries, error descriptions, etc. The
     orchestrator reads this prose to know what you did. Do not skip
     it — empty-body envelopes are useless.

  2. AT TURN END — one footer tag as the FINAL line of your response (namespaced <|report ...|> delimiters; they are NOT HTML/XML so markdown renderers leave them intact, and the `report` prefix prevents collisions with other plugins using the same syntax):

       <|report kind="<kind>"|>

     The tag is a FOOTER, not a replacement for prose. Your prose from part 2 sits ABOVE the tag. The tag is mandatory; missing it blocks the stop. (Whether a listener is actually armed is verified separately by the manifest — you do not need to declare it in a tag.)

     kind ∈ {progress, question, done, blocked}:
       progress  — turn-end status update for visibility
       question  — you need an answer from operator/orchestrator
       done      — task complete; orchestrator may mark shipped
       blocked   — external blocker; orchestrator should escalate

     Tag attributes:
       <|report kind="<kind>" summary="<short>" reply-to="<id>"|>

     • summary="<short sentence>" — STRONGLY RECOMMENDED on every turn. The lead's /list-members view reads `lastSummary` from your manifest; an empty/null value makes the dashboard useless. If you omit it the Stop hook will synthesize one from the first line of your prose, but yours will be better. Keep it ≤ ~120 chars.
     • reply-to="<consumed-message-id>" — REQUIRED when this turn is responding to a message that was just delivered to your mailbox. Use the `id` field from the envelope. This is what wakes the original sender's listener: without it, the lead has to poll.

When a mailbox message arrives, your turn MUST resolve it before ending:
  • REPLY: include `reply-to="<message-id>"` on your `<|report ...|>` tag
  • ACK:   add `<|report ack="<message-id>" reason="why no action"|>` to
           your turn text (for messages you choose not to act on)

You can express your engagement with mailbox messages more precisely
using `decision`:
  - `replied` (implied by reply-to match)
  - `ack-no-action` (saw it, no action — give a reason)
  - `deferred` (will handle next turn — max 3 deferrals per message)
  - `unable` (can't process — operator will see in audit log)

Examples:
  <|report ack="msg-1" decision="ack-no-action" reason="not relevant"|>
  <|report ack="msg-2" decision="deferred" reason="finishing build first"|>
  <|report ack="msg-3" decision="unable" reason="binary attachment not supported"|>

Bare `ack` (no decision attribute) defaults to `ack-no-action`.
Notification envelopes (thread fan-out, member-joined, etc.) are auto-
exempt — you do not need to ack them.

EXAMPLE — a spontaneous status update (no inbound message):

    All tests still green. Awaiting next instruction.

    <|report kind="progress" summary="tests green; idle"|>

EXAMPLE — a turn that finished real work:

    Migrated happy-server/src/auth/ to remove userId scoping (commit a1b2c3d).
    All 42 tests passing. Cross-package typecheck green.

    <|report kind="done" summary="migrated auth, 42 tests green"|>

EXAMPLE — a reply to a mailbox message with id="d45b635a-...":

    Four.

    <|report kind="done" summary="answered 2+2" reply-to="d45b635a-7809-43d8-9977-3556d4598a48"|>

EXAMPLE — a turn that needs an answer:

    I can merge into either main or release-2.7. Which do you want?

    <|report kind="question" summary="merge target: main or release-2.7?"|>

When the listener exits and you resume:
   1. Inspect the background listener task output first; do NOT re-arm if type === arm-skipped.
   2. If mail was delivered, run /crews-review-mail, or the equivalent bash command: node $env:CREWS_BIN review-mail audit-test-member --crew audit-test-crew --cwd 'D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.worktrees/plugins-copilot-cross-engine-audit/.ralph/jobs/plugins-copilot-cross-engine-audit/scratch-crew/state'
   3. Act on every delivered entry, then write prose and end with the kind tag.

Rules:
- Your name is "audit-test-member" — use it verbatim in the listener command.
- ALWAYS write prose — even one short sentence — before the kind tag. Empty-body envelopes are uninformative.
- Valid kinds: progress, question, done, blocked. Do not invent others.
- Mailbox semantics: messages are delivered in batches; use /crews-review-mail to inspect pending entries before acting.

Slash commands available to this member (bare form like `/spawn-member` also works):
  /crews-assign-role member --crew <crew> --name <name> | lead --crew <crew> --name <name> | none | status — Assign this session as a lead or existing member, clear the role, or show role status.
  /crews-join-crew <crew> --as <name> — Join or create a crew as a member and subscribe to the general thread.
  /crews-leave-crew — Leave the current crew, archive pending mailbox messages, and clear this session role.
  /crews-list-members [--all-crews] — Snapshot members visible to your role in the current crew, or every crew with --all-crews.
  /crews-list-crews — List workspace crews and their lead actors.
  /crews-list-threads — List threads in the current crew with message and subscriber counts.
  /crews-peek-mailbox — Preview the first pending mailbox envelope without consuming it.
  /crews-review-mail [--peek] [--since <seq>] — Review inbox-history entries that require attention and advance the reviewed cursor only to surfaced rows.
  /crews-thread-path <thread> — Print the on-disk JSONL path for a crew thread.
  /crews-status — Show this session role, crew, and last-activity status.
  /crews-create-thread <name> [--description "..."] — Create a crew thread and subscribe the current actor to it.
  /crews-send-to-thread <thread> <message> [--reply-to <id>] — Append a message to a crew thread and fan out thread notifications to subscribers.
  /crews-subscribe-thread <thread> — Subscribe the current actor to a crew thread.
  /crews-unsubscribe-thread <thread> — Remove the current actor from a crew thread subscription list.

Use slash commands directly. Exception: /crews-review-mail may be run via the exact bash command above when a listener exit needs inspection. Other CLI mirrors under tools/ exist for external scripting, not for in-session use; if you need a tool's usage just run it with --help.
